text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert — high GPU memory pressure detected on runtime-1 (us-west-2). Creating incident channel #inc-4129990011. Severity: S2.


sara_oncall: I'm oncall. I see a steady increase in allocator failures since 04:12 UTC. Starting live triage.


sara_oncall: Customer-facing symptom: ~5% 500s and tail latency spikes to 1.2s for generate-stream. Not widespread but persistent across a subset of GPU pools.


miguel_sre: I can join. Posting high-level metrics I'm seeing in the past 20m: GPU memory free dropping to <200MB on some hosts, DRM page faults up, and eviction events spiking.


miguel_sre: paste of recent output from node telemetry:

```
node runtime-1-3: GPU0 total 40GB used 39.5GB free 0.5GB active_allocs=312k evictions=128 page_faults=260
node runtime-1-7: GPU1 total 80GB used 78.6GB free 1.4GB active_allocs=498k evictions=3 page_faults=14
-- pattern: small fleet of 40GB machines saturating, 80GB ones less impacted
```


tom_eng_runtime: Hypothesis 1: KV-prefix cache growth per-request + large batch sizes causing fragmentation and inability to satisfy transient allocation patterns.


sara_oncall: Agreed. We saw cache growth post-04:05 after a deploy that increased default batch_size from 8->12 for generate-stream. Rolling that back now to 8 on canary.


incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollback-started by sara_oncall for service=generate-stream commit=ae12b3d


maya_prod_support: Noted inbound customer tickets from 3 enterprise customers observing timeouts ~04:15-04:40 UTC. Escalated to CS. @jess_customer_success on the notification list.


jess_customer_success: ACK. Reaching out to customer owners; will provide interim mitigation notes: reduced batch size + enabling rapid eviction.


miguel_sre: While rollback runs, let's capture detailed allocator traces. Can someone run the mem-sampler on two affected 40GB hosts and one healthy 80GB host? Command: `sudo /opt/redwood/bin/mem-sampler --gpu --span 60`


miguel_sre: Also drop the KV-cache stats: `curl -s http://localhost:9001/debug/kvstats`


tom_eng_runtime: I grabbed kvstats from runtime-1-3:

```
{prefix_cache_items: 1.2M, avg_prefix_len: 312, cache_hits: 1.1M, cache_misses: 420k, evicted_items: 128, total_allocated_bytes: 39_200_000_000}
```


tom_eng_runtime: Notable: avg_prefix_len jumped from ~180 to ~312 in the last 10m. That matches the new prompt template which concatenates user metadata. This increases per-request KV footprint.


sara_oncall: Live mitigation applied: 1) rolled batch_size back to 8 on canary pool, 2) enabled aggressive prefix cache eviction policy (ttl 30s -> 8s) via feature-flag for affected hosts, 3) temporarily route new traffic away from 40GB fleet by policy.


incident-bot: routing-service: traffic-shift: started -> 70% -> 80% to 80GB-pool.


miguel_sre: After mitigation: GPU free on runtime-1-3 rose to ~4GB within 3 minutes; page_faults reduced. Latency tail began to normalize.


maya_prod_support: Customer update: three customers confirmed improvement after 04:25 UTC. One still saw intermittent 502s — asking for logs.


tom_eng_runtime: Actionable hypothesis list in-thread:
- H1: Increased default batch_size post-deploy increased peak working set causing fragmentation on 40GB cards.
- H2: New prompt templates increased average prefix length, raising per-request KV footprint and cache growth.
- H3: Older allocator behavior + fragmentation reduces ability to coalesce free blocks (exacerbated by smaller card size).


miguel_sre: Logs shared for timeline building: attaching snippets (pasted) from 04:06 - 04:20 UTC showing eviction spikes and allocation failures.

```
04:06:11 runtime-1-3 kernel: allocator: allocate failed 640MB order=3
04:07:02 runtime-1-3 runtime: eviction triggered for prefix=customer-xyz keys=42 reclaimed=128MB
04:09:14 runtime-1-3 runtime: allocation success 8MB after split
04:12:33 runtime-1-3 runtime: allocation failed 1.2GB order=4 -> OOM fallback triggered
```


sara_oncall: Timeline so far:
- 04:02 deploy rolled with batch_size=12 default.
- 04:05 traffic increase + new prompt template rollout.
- 04:06 first allocator failures on 40GB hosts.
- 04:12 customer-facing errors spike.
- 04:18 rollback and eviction policy change.
- 04:24 traffic shift complete, metrics improving.


jess_customer_success: I'll consolidate the customer-facing timeline and include mitigation steps we took (rollback, eviction, routing).


miguel_sre: Next steps (short):
- Collect full mem-sampler traces and heap histograms from affected hosts (miguel -> assigned).
- Run fragmentation analyzer on allocator dumps (tom -> assigned).
- Reproduce locally with synthetic load and new prompt template + batch_size=12 to measure working set (tom + eng-ml).
- Consider short-term permanent guardrail: cap batch_size per SKU (40GB cards) to <=8.


sara_oncall: I'm updating the incident doc and will set follow-up postmortem if we confirm allocator fragmentation root cause. For now incident status: mitigated, monitoring.


incident-bot: incident-status: mitigated -> monitoring; channel will remain open for RCA artifacts.


miguel_sre: One more datapoint: host runtime-1-7 (80GB) had much lower evictions despite similar traffic — supports card-size hypothesis not all traffic pattern related.


sara_oncall: Thanks everyone. If no new regressions by 05:00 UTC, I'll close the live page and hand to oncall RCA owners. Tom and Miguel, please start collecting artifacts into the incident runbook.


tom_eng_runtime: Will do. Pushing mem-sampler + allocator dumps to /incidents/4129990011/artifacts and linking in the doc.


jess_customer_success: Sending short customer note now.


maya_prod_support: resolved for most customers; keeping watch.


sara_oncall: last check: 04:35 metrics show error rate back to baseline, GPU free normalized on canary. Marking last_message_ts 4129990375.
